What did the json-c bug hunt find?

Long image

A

Answer

The bug hunt found 8 new bugs in json-c's tokener at commit d2ce61e, and all 8 still reproduce on the baseline today. They sit in less-used paths: comments, VALIDATE_UTF8, STRICT mode, input split across calls, out-of-memory handling and threads. The gate treats the baseline as the specification, so a refactor must keep every one of them.

  1. Findings 1, 2 and 4 give a wrong result, and 3, 3b and 5 report the wrong error. Findings 6, 7 and 8 are about time, memory and threads.1
  2. The search combined reference oracles, metamorphic relations, libFuzzer with sanitizers, fault injection and exhaustive boundary sets.
  3. It also re-found issues that were already open upstream (PRs #1006, #1007, #1014), which shows the harnesses work.2
  4. Its mutation analysis showed which checks a Role A gate needs, and shaped oracle/recorder.c.3

Applies tojson-c master d2ce61e (2026-11-21)findings from bughunt/README.mdreproducers re-run 2026-11-24 on ASan, -O2 and ThreadSanitizer builds of the baseline

1

What are the 8 findings?

Each row shows the reproducer's input and what the baseline did when re-run on 2026-11-24.

FindingInput and what json-c doesWhat it should do
1. Open comment at the end of a container[1,2/* returns success with the value 2Fail with "unexpected end of data", as [1,2 does4
2. Even run of stars before //** doc **/ 1 fails; [1 /***/ ] returns 1Parse both; the second is [1]5
3. UTF-8 character after a value{"a":1}é with STRICT, ALLOW_TRAILING_CHARS and VALIDATE_UTF8 fails with "invalid utf-8 string"Succeed, as {"a":1}x does6
3b. Syntax error on a UTF-8 character[é] with VALIDATE_UTF8 says "invalid utf-8 string"Say "unexpected character", as without the flag7
4. Single-quoted key in STRICT mode{'a':1} returns {"a":1}Reject it, as ['a'] is rejected8
5. Out of memory on a top-level valuetrue or -12 with a failed allocation says "unexpected end of data"Say "out of memory", as [true] does9
6. Long number fed in small pieces640,000 digits in 1-byte calls take 3.58 s; a string of the same length takes 0.01 sTake linear time10
7. Long comment fed in pieces100 MB of comment in 64 KiB calls peaks at 101 MB of memory; whitespace peaks at 1.7 MBUse constant memory11
8. First calls from two threadsThreadSanitizer reports a data race on the cached C locale (lines 357 and 359), 5 of 5 runsNo race12

Doubling the number's length multiplies the time by about 4: 0.221 → 0.881 → 3.583 s. That is quadratic growth, while the string stays linear.

2

Why does each bug happen?

FindingCause in json_tokener_parse_exFound by
1The comment states jump to out: at the end of input. The end-of-input check passes because saved_state is still finish from the inner value.Stream oracle: two documents on one tokener
2comment_end sends any byte other than /, including a second *, back to comment, which then skips one byteInserting a comment between tokens must not change the result
3, 3bPEEK_CHAR validates the byte after a value without consuming it. out: turns the pending multi-byte count into a UTF-8 error.Reading the validator; a BOM test from the literature review
4The STRICT check for ' was added to start in 2013 but not to object_field_startSTRICT json-c against Python's json on JSONTestSuite
5A top-level value is built only when the NUL arrives, and the end-of-input check at out: overwrites the memory errorFailing the Nth allocation for every N
6On every resume, number searches all saved digits for e and E with strchrTiming one-shot against 1-byte feeding per token type
7The comment states append every comment byte to pb, which only debug output readsMutation analysis: removing those appends changes no result
8c_numeric_locale is created on first use without a lock (commit fd92d58, after release 0.19)ThreadSanitizer with two concurrent first calls

Finding 1 has a second effect, found during the gate review on 2026-11-24 and not yet in the bug hunt notes. If the caller keeps parsing on the same tokener after the false success, [[1/* followed by """" leaks a 57-byte string.

3

How was the tokener searched?

Diagram structure
  • Inputs and corpora inputs
  • Compare with references oracles
  • Metamorphic relations relations
  • Fuzz with sanitizers fuzz
  • Faults, time, threads faults
  • Minimal reproducer repro
  • Search upstream upstream
  • Fix locally, rerun fix
  • faults → repro
  • fuzz → repro
  • inputs → faults
  • inputs → fuzz
  • inputs → oracles
  • inputs → relations
  • oracles → repro
  • relations → repro
  • repro → upstream
  • upstream → fix · new
  1. Inputs and corpora ↗

    A grammar-based generator, fuzz corpora, JSONTestSuite and exhaustive sets: 2.37M UTF-8 sequences and 147,620 short number strings.

  2. Compare with references ↗

    STRICT json-c against Python's json (120k inputs), lenient json-c against a Python model of its grammar (200k), and 0.18 / 0.19 / master against each other (111k). Found finding 4.

  3. Metamorphic relations ↗

    Rules that must hold without knowing the answer: split input equals one-shot input; an inserted comment changes nothing; wrapping x as [x] keeps its value; stricter flags never accept more; equal escapes give equal strings. Found findings 1 and 2.

  4. Fuzz with sanitizers ↗

    Four libFuzzer targets, each also checking a relation, under ASan and UBSan: for example about 46 million runs of the len = -1 target in 10 minutes. Plus MemorySanitizer, a 32-bit build and unsigned char. No crash.

  5. Faults, time, threads ↗

    Failing every allocation in turn (finding 5), timing per token type (finding 6), measuring memory (finding 7) and ThreadSanitizer (finding 8).

  6. Minimal reproducer ↗

    Each finding got a small repro_*.c file in bughunt/.

  7. Search upstream ↗

    Searched json-c issues and pull requests on 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-22: none of the 8 findings was reported.

  8. Fix locally, rerun ↗

    local_fixes_findings_1-5.patch fixes findings 1–5. With it, json-c's own tests give the same result as master, and every harness runs clean.

4

What else did it turn up?

These were noted but not claimed as bugs, because the right behaviour is a judgement call or already known.13

KindWhat was seen
Already open upstreamA UTF-8 character split across calls fails with VALIDATE_UTF8 (PR #1014). A number split across calls loses or replaces parts: [12 + -3] gives [12] (PR #1006). A key with \u0000 is cut short (PR #1007).
Design limitSTRICT rejects 1 2 in one call but returns 1 when the input is split after the space
ObservationLone surrogate escapes all become U+FFFD, so distinct keys collide and members are silently dropped
ObservationA top-level STRICT 01, 1. or 1e says "unexpected end of data" instead of "number expected"
ObservationThe header's json_tokener_parse_ex example checks trailing characters in a way that reports them for every input
Observationnull returns NULL with success, although the header says a valid value always gives an object

The re-found upstream issues matter: the harnesses discovered them on their own, so they can find real bugs.2

CheckSizeResult

Flag monotonicity38,835 files0 violations

MemorySanitizer and a 32-bit buildAll corporaClean
Line and branch coverage of json_tokener.c7 feeding modes × 6 flag sets90.8% lines, 85.1% branches; the rest is mostly out-of-memory code

"Clean" means these checks found nothing new beyond the 8 findings, not that the tokener has no other bugs.14

6

How strong would a gate built from these harnesses be?

226 of the 248 compiling mutants were killed (91.1%). An earlier run killed 130 of 150 (86.7%).1516 The README's "89%" matches both runs combined: 356 of 398 = 89.4%.

Lesson from the survivorsWhere it went
Compare the type of every value, not just its textThe recorder's type signature, including exact doubles
Include a mode where one tokener reads several inputsThe recorder's reuse mode
Add boundary inputs for every range checkoracle/inputs/core.txt is this input set, boundary inputs included
4 mutants die only when input is splitNot yet in the gate; the 2026-11-24 review measured the gap
7

What happens to these bugs now?

Keep, then report

For the refactoring experiment the 8 findings are part of the specification. Fixing one is a change in behaviour, and the gate's own tests plant fixes for findings 1–4 to prove it notices. Reporting them upstream with the reproducers and the local patch is planned for week 15, as Role C's work.
